Any disruption in the services of these trading members or our inability to onboard new trading members could have an adverse impact on our operations.

Disruptions, failures, or inadequacies in our IT infrastructure, systems, or software, including those provided by third- party vendors, could adversely affect our business, reputation and results of operations, and may subject us to regulatory action or the imposition of financial disincentives by SEBI.
Any disruption, whether from software malfunctions, connectivity failures, or order-matching errors, has the potential to affect market integrity and investor confidence at scale.

Any failure, inadequacy, or disruption of our IT infrastructure, whether due to hardware or software defects or malfunctions, cyberattacks, phishing, distributed denial-of-service attacks, operational or human error, insufficient capacity, natural disasters, power outages, disruptions in telecommunications services, unauthorised access, fraud, military or political conflicts, terrorist attacks, computer viruses, ransomware, malware, or issues with third-party service providers, could significantly disrupt our business operations and erode market confidence.
For example, our critical systems have, in the past, experienced disruptions that have led to the shutdown of our operations for a few hours.

We have since implemented remedial measures, including architectural change of system design, shifting from SAN-based to host-based replication in key systems, strengthening disaster recovery and redundancy, adding additional service providers for replication links, and limiting link utilisation to safeguard failover capacity.

Prospective investors should pay particular attention to the fact that our Company is incorporated under the laws of India and is subject to a legal and regulatory environment which may differ in certain respects from that of other countries.

Redseer is an independent consultant with respect to our Company and its associates, and is not a related party of our Company, Directors, Key Management Personnel, members of the Senior Management or the Book Running Lead Managers.

Our operations and growth prospects are intrinsically tied to government policy decisions and regulatory direction across capital market reforms, disinvestment programmes, foreign direct investment, and financial inclusion initiatives.
While supportive government and regulatory action have historically expanded market access and driven trading activity on our platform, policy interventions can also be restrictive.
Adverse regulatory developments have also had an impact on our specific businesses, including our currency derivatives and Bank Nifty derivatives offerings.
There can be no assurance that further fiscal or regulatory measures of a similar nature will not be introduced in the future.

We cannot predict future government policies or regulatory actions, or the terms on which they may be implemented, and any adverse change in government policy or regulation could have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations, financial condition, and prospects.

In Fiscal 2026, our revenue from transaction charges decreased by 4.24% primarily due to a decrease in ADTV across cash market, equity futures and equity options products, reflecting macro-regulatory measures introduced during Fiscal 2026 to strengthen the equity index derivatives framework.
This concentration exposes us to risks specific to the derivatives market, including those arising from changes in regulation, market sentiment, and participant behaviour.
Also see “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations – Significant Factors affecting Our Financial Condition and Results of Operations” on page 398.
Further, our business is indirectly exposed to regulatory actions and developments affecting brokers and trading members that access our platform.

SEBI's heightened scrutiny of intermediary conduct reflects an increasingly robust compliance and enforcement environment, and any regulatory action or operational restriction imposed on trading members could limit investors’ ability or willingness to participate actively in the market.
We operate in a highly regulated industry, primarily overseen by SEBI.

All such findings are reviewed by our respective Regulatory Oversight Committees, Public Interest Directors Committee (“PID Committee”), and Governing Board, and we are required to implement timely corrective actions to address the identified regulatory concerns.

SEBI conducts regular periodic inspections on various aspects of our operations, including our (i) internal controls, systems and processes, (ii) risk management systems, (iii) policies, (iv) management and governance framework, and (v) other operational matters.

Pursuant to past SEBI inspections, we have also been subject to enforcement actions and, if material deficiencies are detected, such enforcement actions may include suspending or restricting our trading activities, prohibiting the launch of new products or services, imposing significant monetary penalties, or debarment of our Company, Directors, or Key Management Personnel from accessing the securities market.
